conventions.convention: Weight matrices have shape d_l by d_(l-1); fan-in is d_(l-1), fan-out is d_l, and backward multiplication uses the transpose.
Symmetry means equality in distribution of Z and -Z. Zero atoms are allowed; positive and negative sign probabilities are each (1-p_0)/2.
PReLU is t for t>0 and at for t≤0. Its specified gate at zero is c; this is an ordinary derivative at zero only when a=c=1.
ReLU backward signals use the zero-at-kink gate 1_(Z>0). At zero preactivations they are specified backpropagation signals, without an assertion of ordinary differentiability.
Forward preservation concerns centered preactivation variance, using activation second moments. The raw-input first layer has no preceding rectifier factor; repeated half factors start at layer 2.

G_l denotes a common downstream second moment, including an uncentered terminal signal. Backward preservation formulas require gate/signal independence and independence of the whole weight matrix from the gated signal.

load_bearing.statement: For mutually independent centered square-integrable real weights W_i of variances σ_i² and a real random vector X with square-integrable coordinates independent of the whole weight vector, S=Σ_i W_iX_i is square-integrable, E[S]=0, and Var(S)=Σ_i σ_i²E[X_i²]. The coordinates of X need not be mutually independent.

For symmetric real Z with p_0=P(Z=0), each strict sign has probability (1-p_0)/2. If E[Z²]<∞, E[ReLU(Z)]=E[|Z|]/2, E[ReLU(Z)²]=E[Z²]/2, E[φ_a(Z)]=(1-a)E[|Z|]/2, and E[φ_a(Z)²]=(1+a²)E[Z²]/2. Var(ReLU(Z))=E[Z²]/2−E[|Z|]²/4. Without a moment hypothesis, E[η_(a,c)(Z)²]=(1+a²)(1-p_0)/2+c²p_0.

For the specified zero-at-kink backward signals, square-integrable summands T_ji=W_(l,ji)γ_(l,j)g_(l,j) give the exact mean sum and variance/covariance sum without independence. Additionally, independent symmetric centered weight entries of common variance σ_l², symmetric preactivations of common zero probability p_l, common downstream second moment G_l, gate-vector/downstream-signal independence, and weight-matrix/gated-signal independence give centered upstream coordinates with G_(l-1)=(1-p_l)d_lσ_l²G_l/2, and the corresponding finite product when these hypotheses hold at every layer. For l≥2 with ReLU inputs and σ_l²>0, weight-matrix/gated-signal independence forces h_l=0 almost surely; gate independence and p_l<1 then force G_l=0.

For the stated finite zero-bias ReLU stack with independent symmetric centered IID layer weights independent of their layer inputs, common finite input-coordinate second moments, and symmetric preactivations, Var(Z_(l,j))=n_lσ_l²Var(Z_(l-1,1))/2 for 2≤l≤L. The raw-input relation is Var(Z_(1,j))=n_1σ_1²E[X_(0,1)²], and V_L=V_1∏_(l=2)^L(n_lσ_l²/2). Input coordinates may be dependent and zero atoms are allowed.

For n≥1 IID symmetric real Z_i with no atom at zero, X_i=ReLU(Z_i), and arbitrary real random weights on the same probability space, T=Σ_i W_iX_i satisfies P(T=0)≥2^(-n)>0. The same conclusion holds if only the X_i are mutually independent and each Z_i is symmetric with no atom at zero.

Under the stated PReLU forward assumptions, the hidden-layer forward coefficient is (1+a²)n_lσ_l²/2. Under the additional backward gate/signal and weight/gated-signal independence assumptions, the backward coefficient is d_lσ_l²κ_l, where κ_l=(1+a²)(1-p_l)/2+c_l²p_l. The forward scale is 2/((1+a²)n_l); the atomless conditional backward scale is 2/((1+a²)d_l). With atoms the conditional backward-preserving scale is 1/(d_lκ_l) when κ_l>0; κ_l=0 gives zero upstream variance for every finite weight variance.

published_dependencies.used_for: Expectation as a probability-space integral and direct discrete or density-based moment calculations.
Centered variance and covariance definitions, including the unconditional backward covariance expansion.
Whole-vector independence, coordinate independence, and inheritance through generated sigma-algebras.
Measurability of finite sums, products, squares, and coordinate-product maps.
Finite independent-family product laws and probabilities of simultaneous sign or zero events.
Independence of measurable functions of separate independent random vectors.
Factoring integrable products and nonnegative squared products under the explicitly stated independence assumptions.
Finite-sum expectation expansions, variance expansions, and almost-sure order.
L²-to-L¹ integrability and integrability of pairwise products.
Transferring symmetry of laws to activation moments and sign probabilities.
Ordinary backward gradients at differentiable realizations, separately from specified kink conventions.
